findings.summary: Information reaches the reader only after a refusal. A conditional reader-brief section would give the stage order on the first read, which is what the root-cause generator now prefers.
findings.evidence: root_cause_request_at now tells the job to 'change the code so that information is given to it ... Prefer this over any rule that refuses work.' The reader brief already has request-dependent sections (referenced_jobs_section, earlier_attempt_section) that are not part of the always-loaded rule list. Decision 1 rejects only a READING_RULES line or a prompt edit (2 tokens left), not a section shown when the trigger fires. As planned, every speed request costs one refused read, and a second refusal fails the request (reader.rs:399-401). The accepted reading excludes prompt and brief files, so this cannot be changed inside this job. Fix: In D190, state that the refusal is the chosen mechanism under the accepted reading. Name a follow-up: a conditional reader-brief section listing the StageMinutes stage order and where the medians are printed, shown when check_timing_claim's trigger matches the request.

findings.summary: T1 (a cut verb plus a figure) refuses plain timeout or interval changes that make no stage-timing claim.
findings.evidence: 'Reduce the timeout to 30 seconds' and 'cut the poll interval to 5 seconds' are behavior changes to a setting, and T1 fires on them. The plan accepts this as a risk. Yet every class example the plan lists for a cut verb also contains a TIME word or a STAGE noun ('Reduce the CI wait from 10 minutes', 'Reduce time spent waiting for CI'). Fix: Require a TIME word or a STAGE noun in the same segment for the CUT branch of T1. Add an Accept corpus case for 'Reduce the timeout to 30 seconds'.
findings.location: Plan Decision 3 (T1 with the CUT list); Risks bullet 1

findings.summary: 'times' as a TIME word also means a count.
findings.evidence: With T3 (CUT + TIME + STAGE), 'Reduce the number of times the check runs' fires. 'times' is counted as duration, although here it is a count. Fix: Drop 'times' from TIME, or skip it when the words before it are 'number of', and add that phrase to the leave-alone unit test.

findings.summary: The dependents list omits the steward's throughput design request, which carries 'Predicted saving: N minutes'.
findings.evidence: throughput_request writes 'Predicted saving: {:.1} minutes per landed job', which matches T1 (saving + figure). Its deliverables are docs/design/ only, so a design-class reading closes the gate (surveys.rs:237-245). The plan names slowdown_request and root_cause_request but not this generator. Fix: Add throughput_request to the dependents with the reason it is unaffected (design class, gate closed), or add an Accept corpus case built from it.
findings.location: Plan Dependents ('requests Athena generates and the reader then reads'); crates/athena-core/src/hestia.rs:2257-2293

findings.summary: The number of new corpus cases is stated as 20, but Decision 7 lists 17 new cases plus one changed expectation.
findings.evidence: Decision 7 enumerates new cases (1)-(6), (8), (10)-(16), (17) twice and (18), which is 17 new; (7) is changed and (9) is unchanged. Fix: State the actual count, or note that the figure is a tally to be recounted, as decision 7 already does for INPUT_FORMS.
findings.location: Plan Step 6, Demonstration for criterion 4, Dependents (refusal corpus)

findings.summary: The duration-figure counter must read decimals such as '45.0 min'.
findings.evidence: slowdown_request formats minutes with {:.1} (hestia.rs:2391-2402). A counter that matches only integers would count no figures from that text, which matters for Timeline part (b) if a reader copies the medians. Fix: Let the number part accept an optional decimal fraction, and include '45.0 min' in a unit test.
findings.location: Plan Decision 3 (duration figure) and the steward slowdown cases

summary: Round 2 resolves round 1's only major finding. The trigger is now built from the class: inflections are listed, and reduce, cut and save verbs, time words and stage nouns are added. Each existing Accept case is decided on purpose, and the minors are answered (narrowed exemption, real example path at crates/athena-core/src/run/mod.rs, error text pointing at the `athena status` medians, INPUT_FORMS length 77, Criterion-wrapped declaration). I checked the named code in the snapshot: is_generated_line and ROOT_CAUSE_ANCHOR (terms.rs:52-80, pub(super)), the step! list (checks.rs:534-549), StageMinutes::named (throughput.rs:113, six stages ending 'landing and rebuild'), the public generators slowdown_request and root_cause_request (hestia.rs:2381, 1012), the 63-entry INPUT_FORMS with the reused tags present (refusal_corpus.rs:90-119), the ci-wait cases (474, 483), and the assert_ne! unit test (reading.rs:8642-8691). All match the plan. The demonstrations call the real gate through refuser_for, check_reading_text and the corpus, and would fail without the step! line or with the narrower trigger. Remaining findings are minor. The refusal-first design gives the reader the stage order only after a refusal, where a conditional reader-brief section would give it on the first read; the accepted reading's scope excludes that. Trigger T1 will refuse plain timeout or interval changes, and 'times' has a count sense. throughput_request is missing from the dependents list but its readings are not gated. The case count is stated as 20 where 17 new cases are listed.
